code.text: Structured present-day safety assessment

resource.valueString: Current ideation absent; intent absent; plan absent; access reviewed true. Disposition: Outpatient care with close follow-up. He has no thoughts of suicide or self-harm now and has had none. Because he is ill, isolated, far from home and screening in the moderate range, his risk factors were reviewed with him privately and a written safety plan was made: his warning signs (not sleeping, not eating, not wanting to see anyone), what helps, who he can call, and the clinic number. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline was given and saved in his phone. Lethal-means counseling: no firearm; medicines dispensed in short supplies. Safety reviewed at every visit.

note.text: Synthetic assessment. Historical evidence is not represented as current behavior.

description.text: A diagnosis within days, with tuberculosis either confirmed or excluded before any treatment that could hide it

outcomeCode.text: Amebic liver abscess diagnosed at the second visit; active tuberculosis excluded by the radiograph, three smears, NAAT and cultures at six weeks

description.text: No fever, the abscess treated, and the luminal course completed

outcomeCode.text: Afebrile by the third day of metronidazole; paromomycin completed; CRP and liver tests normal

description.text: Regain at least half of the lost weight within three months, on a diet that keeps his rules

outcomeCode.text: 52.0 to 56.6 kg, nearly all the weight lost

description.text: Vitamin B12 and vitamin D in the normal range and the anemia resolved

outcomeCode.text: B12 520 pg/mL; 25-hydroxyvitamin D 32 ng/mL; hemoglobin 13.8 g/dL

description.text: PHQ-9 below 10 with no thoughts of self-harm, and regular contact with people who matter to him

outcomeCode.text: PHQ-9 12 to 5; weekly calls home and a weekly meal with others from his community

description.text: Complete four months of rifampin for latent tuberculosis infection

outcomeCode.text: Month two of four; no side effects; liver tests normal

SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Infectious diseases consultation at the second visit for fever, weight loss and right upper quadrant pain in a young man from South India with a history of dysentery, to interpret the tuberculosis and amebiasis tests, the imaging, and the choice and order of treatment
  • Tuberculosis evaluation before any antibiotic: chest radiograph, three induced sputum samples for acid-fast smear, NAAT and mycobacterial culture, an interferon-gamma release assay, and HIV testing; airborne precautions until three smears are negative
  • Liver and gut evaluation: abdominal ultrasound tomorrow morning, Entamoeba histolytica serology, stool antigen or PCR and microscopy, two sets of blood cultures, liver tests and CRP
  • Nutrition: vitamin B12, folate, ferritin and 25-hydroxyvitamin D measured; weight at every visit; a dietitian visit to plan meals within his vegetarian diet and his rules
  • Mood and safety: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at least monthly while symptoms last; structured safety assessment and a written safety plan with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; safety reviewed at every visit; short-term counseling with the university counseling service, at times he chooses
  • Support far from home: the university's international student office and his department's graduate office about leave and deadlines while he is ill; a regular time to call his family; introductions, at his wish, to the local Tamil association and a Hindu temple community with shared meals; a letter for his fellowship about his illness
  • Acetaminophen for fever and pain, no more than 3 g a day; nothing else until the results are known
  • Cold: rest, fluids, warm salt-water gargles, honey in warm water and acetaminophen; continue rifampin; no antibiotic; return for fever over three days, right upper quadrant pain, or breathlessness
  • As the infectious diseases physician advised: metronidazole 750 mg three times a day for 10 days, then paromomycin 500 mg three times a day for 7 days, not taken together; no aspiration unless fever persists after 72 hours, the abscess grows, or rupture threatens; a nurse phone check on the third day; no repeat imaging if he recovers
  • Vitamin B12 1,000 micrograms by mouth daily and vitamin D 50,000 units weekly for 8 weeks, then 2,000 units daily; a dietitian plan within his rules: protein from dal, chickpeas, beans, milk, curd and paneer; dairy and fortified foods for B12; batch cooking once a day for two meals; easy foods such as curd rice and khichdi on tired days; an Indian grocery delivery
  • Latent tuberculosis infection, once cultures were negative and the liver tests normal: rifampin 600 mg daily for 4 months, with a monthly clinical check for nausea, rash, jaundice and adherence; liver tests at baseline and at two months because of the recent liver disease; orange body fluids explained

resource.title: Srinivasa Ramanujan synthetic care plan
resource.description: The evaluation of fever, weight loss and right upper quadrant pain in a 29-year-old mathematician from Tamil Nadu, a strict vegetarian, who came to a research fellowship far from home. The episode works through the differential that divided his historical physicians and later historians, tuberculosis or amebiasis, with modern tests: a chest radiograph, induced sputum for smears, NAAT and culture, an interferon-gamma release assay, stool tests and Entamoeba histolytica serology, and an abdominal ultrasound. The single modern diagnosis is an amebic liver abscess, treated by CDC guidance with metronidazole and then the luminal agent paromomycin; the positive IGRA with negative cultures is latent tuberculosis infection, treated after the abscess with four months of rifampin under the 2020 NTCA/CDC guideline, with the ATS/CDC/IDSA guidelines for diagnosis and treatment. The episode adds a nutrition assessment with vitamin B12 and vitamin D repletion suited to a lacto-vegetarian, a dietary plan built on his own food and rules, PHQ-9 and GAD-7 screening with a structured safety assessment, counseling, and practical support for a student far from home. The modern diagnosis is synthetic and does not settle the historical question.
